title: Erdős #14: Unique Representation Sums
description: Formalizes Erdős Problem #14: estimate the count U(N) of integers not uniquely representable as a sum of two elements from A ⊆ ℕ. Introduces repCount, uniqueSums, nonUniqueCount predicates. Axiomatizes Erdős's construction (U(N) << N^{1/2+ε}), Erdős-Freud finite bound, and the lower bound holding infinitely often. Proves Sidon sets have all sums unique and are sparse. 6 theorems, 13 definitions, 3 axioms.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: 3 axioms: erdos_upper_construction (Erdős: ∃ A with U(N) << N^{1/2+ε} for all large N), erdos_lower_infinitely_often (∃ A with U(N) >> N^{1/3-ε} for infinitely many N), erdos_freud_finite (Erdős-Freud: ∃ A ⊆ {1,...,N} with U(N) < 2^{3/2} · N^{1/2}).
originalContributions: repCount: formal count of ways to write n as a+b with a≤b and a,b∈A
uniqueSums / uniqueSums': set of sums representable in exactly one way
nonUniqueCount: U(N) = |{1,...,N} \ B| count of non-uniquely representable integers
IsSidon: predicate — a+b = c+d implies {a,b}={c,d} (all pairwise sums distinct)
sidon_all_unique: Sidon sets have all sums in uniqueSums
sidon_implies_unique_sumset: Sidon ↔ uniqueSums A = sumset A

overview.historicalContext:
Erdős Problem #14 emerged from the study of additive bases and representation functions. A Sidon set (B₂ sequence), introduced by Simon Sidon in 1932, has all pairwise sums distinct — equivalently, every integer has at most one representation as a sum of two elements. Sidon sets achieve U(N) = 0 (all sums are unique), but are limited to size O(√N) by the classical difference argument (k elements produce k(k-1)/2 distinct differences, bounded by N-1).

The tension in Problem #14: can a set have MANY unique sums without being as sparse as a Sidon set? Erdős asked two questions: (a) must U(N) always grow at least as fast as N^{1/2-ε}? (b) can U(N) grow slower than √N? The known results place tight constraints. Erdős constructed a set A achieving U(N) ≤ C·N^{1/2+ε} for every ε > 0, while Erdős and Freud showed explicit finite constructions with U(N) < 2^{3/2}·√N ≈ 2.83√N.

A delicate formalization point: the quantifier structure of question (a) allows C to depend on ε, making it possible that U(N) = √N/log N satisfies both (a) and (b) simultaneously. The genuine resolution requires an Ω(√N) bound — a uniform lower bound. This subtle distinction between 'for each ε, a bound' versus 'a uniform bound' is made explicit in the Lean formalization.
overview.problemStatement: Estimate F(N) = min_A U(N), the minimum non-unique count over all A. Is F(N) >> N^{1/2-ε}? Is F(N) = o(N^{1/2}) possible?
overview.text: For A ⊆ ℕ, define B = {n : n = a+b uniquely with a≤b, a,b∈A}. Let U(N) = |{1,...,N}\B| count non-uniquely representable integers. Sidon sets (all sums distinct) minimize U(N) = 0 but have |A∩[0,N]| = O(N^{1/2}). Erdős asked: how small can U(N) be for general A? The question connects to additive bases and combinatorial number theory.
overview.proofStrategy: Define representation counting infrastructure: repCount, uniqueSums, nonUniqueCount. Prove Sidon characterization. Axiomatize the deep analytic results about optimal construction. Define sumset and non-unique count for the main problem statement.
keyInsights: The Sidon size bound $|A \cap [1,N]| \leq 2\sqrt{N}$ is proved by a difference-injection argument: the $\binom{k}{2}$ pairwise differences of $k$ elements must be distinct (Sidon property) and fit in $\{1,\ldots,N-1\}$, giving $k(k-1)/2 \leq N-1$.

Questions 14a and 14b are genuinely independent as stated due to quantifier sensitivity: 14a allows $C = C(\varepsilon) \to 0$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$, so $U(N) = \sqrt{N}/\log N$ satisfies both. Only an $\Omega(\sqrt{N})$ uniform lower bound would make 14b impossible.

The Erdős-Freud constant $2^{3/2} \approx 2.83$ gives the explicit finite construction bound $U(N) < 2.83\sqrt{N}$, showing that near-Sidon behavior (most sums unique) is achievable even with a dense set.

The difference between $B_2$ sequences (unique sums) and Sidon sets (unique sums, defined via a+b=c+d) is terminological: both require $r_A(n) \leq 1$. The Lean formalization makes this explicit through the `IsSidon` predicate.

The `sidon_diff_injective` lemma is the key technical step: pairwise differences of a Sidon set are all distinct. This is equivalent to the definition but stated in the contrapositive for the size bound proof.

The interaction between Sidon sets and additive bases: Sidon sets minimize U(N) (all sums unique) but can't be additive bases (too sparse). Problem #14 asks how much sparsity can be traded for reduced non-uniqueness.
prerequisites: Additive combinatorics: sumsets, Sidon sets, B₂ sequences
Analytic number theory: density and counting arguments

conclusion.summary: Erdős #14 infrastructure formalized: repCount/uniqueSums/nonUniqueCount predicates, Sidon characterization, Erdős construction and Freud bound axiomatized. 6 theorems, 443 lines, 3 axioms.
conclusion.implications: The unique sum problem connects to Sidon sets and additive bases. Improvements would require formalizing probabilistic construction methods. The problem remains open for the exact growth rate of the optimal U(N).
openQuestions: Prove Erdős's upper construction without axioms using probabilistic methods
Determine if U(N) = o(N^{1/2}) is achievable
Connect to the Sidon set size bound |A∩[0,N]| = O(N^{1/2})

crossReferences.description: Both study additive set problems from Erdős; #28 studies bases, #14 studies unique sums

sections.title: Problem Statement and Background
sections.summary: Full statement of Problem #14a/b, known results (Erdős construction, Erdős-Freud bound), connection to Sidon sets, and references.

sections.title: Part I: Representation Counting
sections.summary: Defines repCount (ways to write n as a+b with a≤b), uniqueSums, uniqueSums' (ExistsUnique formulation), sumset, nonUniqueSums.

sections.title: Part II: Counting Functions
sections.summary: Defines nonUniqueCount A N (the main U(N) function), multiRepCount (sums with ≥2 representations), missingCount (missing sums).

sections.title: Part III: Sidon Sets
sections.summary: Defines IsSidon. Proves sidon_all_unique (Sidon → sumset ⊆ uniqueSums). Helper lemmas: sidon_diff_injective (all pairwise differences distinct), card_strict_pairs (k(k-1)/2 pairs via Prod.swap bijection).

sections.title: Sidon Size Bound
sections.summary: sidon_size_bound: |A ∩ {1,...,N}| ≤ 2√N. Proof: k(k-1)/2 distinct differences in {1,...,N-1} via Sidon injectivity; contradiction for k ≥ 2⌊√N⌋+1.

sections.title: Part IV: The Main Questions
sections.summary: Formalizes erdos_14a (∀A,ε: U(N) ≥ C·N^{1/2-ε} eventually) and erdos_14b (∃A: U(N)/√N → 0). Key formalization note: with current quantifiers, 14a does NOT imply ¬14b.

sections.title: Omega(√N) Implies Not Little-o
sections.summary: omega_sqrt_implies_not_little_o: if ∀A ∃C>0 with U(N) ≥ C·√N eventually, then erdos_14b fails. Proof: contradicts the Tendsto-to-zero condition using a concrete large N.

sections.title: Part V: Known Constructions
sections.summary: Three axioms: erdos_upper_construction (∃A with U(N) ≤ C·N^{1/2+ε} eventually), erdos_lower_infinitely_often (U(N) ≥ C·N^{1/3-ε} for ∃^∞ N), erdos_freud_finite (∀N ∃A with U(N) < 2^{3/2}·√N).

sections.title: Part VI: Examples
sections.summary: empty_repCount (empty set), singleton_uniqueSums ({k} → uniqueSums = {2k}), consecutive_many_nonunique ({1,...,n} has 4 = 1+3 = 2+2 non-uniquely represented).

sections.title: Part VII: Perfect Sidon Sets
sections.summary: IsPerfectSidon: Sidon set whose sumset covers ≥ N integers in {1,...,2N}. perfectSidonExists: asks whether (1-ε)-coverage is achievable for all large N.
